rounds.text: Shanti Gold International Ltd is currently demonstrating elite capital efficiency metrics that tower above industry benchmarks, with an ROA of 21.76%, ROE of 23.42%, and ROCE of 24.85% compared to sector medians of just 4.96%, 8.65%, and 10.27% respectively [E7, E8, E9]. This stellar operational performance is complemented by robust market momentum, reflected in an absolute relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and a 93% compounded share price growth over the past year [E11, E24]. Management is aggressively scaling operations to capture booming structured jewellery demand, backed by explicit guidance for 50% to 60% top-line value growth and 30% to 40% volume growth for the year [E44, E47]. This expansion is supported by tangible physical growth, notably a forthcoming ₹47 crore Jaipur facility across 3 acres slated for operational kickoff around mid-November or December, alongside a ₹100 crore rights issue dedicated to scaling working capital and gold reserves [E50, E51, E52, E60]. Furthermore, the stock trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 17.08x compared to a sector benchmark of 25.68x, offering an undervalued entry point relative to its peer group [E5]. Conceded: Promoter holding decreased by 4.54 percentage points to 70.35% as of September 2026, and the dividend yield sits at 0.00% [E3, E14].

The investment case carries notable structural risks starting with insider dilution, as promoter holdings dropped from 74.89% to 70.35% alongside reductions in foreign and domestic institutional stakes [E14, E15, E16]. Valuation requires caution because the price-to-book ratio sits at an elevated 4.56x compared to the sector benchmark of 2.08x, and the dividend yield is completely absent at 0.00% [E3, E6]. Furthermore, operational momentum displays fragility, evidenced by inconsistent quarterly operating margins and high annualised volatility of 54.8% [E13, E27]. Conceded: [E18].

Conceded: [E3, E14, E15, E16]. While institutional and promoter stakes saw adjustments, institutional money flow overall registers positive with a holding change of +0.36 percentage points, alongside positive screening for institutional inflow [E17, E34]. The elevated price-to-book ratio of 4.56x is justified by extraordinary return metrics, including an ROA of 21.76%, ROE of 23.42%, and ROCE of 24.85%, which massively outperform sector benchmarks of 4.96%, 8.65%, and 10.27% respectively [E6, E7, E8, E9]. Furthermore, the company trades at an attractive P/E of 17.08x compared to the sector benchmark of 25.68x, and an EV/EBITDA of 12.43x against a sector benchmark of 14.44x [E5, E10]. Annualised volatility is offset by a strong Sharpe ratio of 1.08, a relative-strength rating of 100, and solid price momentum with the stock sitting above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E23, E24, E27, E28].

Conceded: [E5, E7, E9, E10, E23, E28, E34]. While those favorable valuation discounts and momentum indicators exist, the bull completely glosses over the severe quality issues hidden beneath the headline returns, such as the alarming fact that annualised volatility sits at an extreme 54.8% [E27]. Furthermore, the bull uses institutional inflow and positive money flow signals [E17, E34] to brush off insider exits, yet actual ownership data proves an exodus: promoters slashed their stake from 74.89% to 70.35%, domestic institutions dropped from 4.01% to 1.64%, and foreign institutions fell from 2.68% to 2.22% over the same period [E14, E16, E15]. The bull's defense of a lofty 4.56x P/B ratio via high ROE and ROCE ignores that a massive portion of recent profitability was inflated by a one-time accounting shift from FIFO to WAC that locked in unrealized inventory gains, providing roughly 2% to 2.5% of artificial elevation to Q1 EBITDA margins [E6, E8, E9, E54]. Finally, citing a relative-strength rating of 100 [E24] and moving average alignment [E23] as permanent safety nets is reckless when the stock trades at 91% of its 52-week range [E21] with a negligible margin of safety of just 3.8% [E19].

Conceded: [E27]. The bear’s concern over insider selling ignores the positive institutional money flow signal (+0.36 percentage points) showing sophisticated buyers absorbing supply [E17, E34], while promoters still retain a commanding majority stake of 70.35% [E14]. The criticism of the P/B ratio [E6] misses that superior operational efficiency—demonstrated by an ROA of 21.76%, ROE of 23.42%, and ROCE of 24.85% against meager sector benchmarks—fully justifies the premium valuation [E7, E8, E9]. Furthermore, while Q1 EBITDA benefited from an inventory valuation change [E54], the company's underlying financial health remains exceptional with an EV/EBITDA of 12.43x trading below the sector benchmark of 14.44x [E10]. Finally, the dismissive stance on momentum and relative strength overlooks a flawless RS rating of 100 alongside strong moving average alignment, which validates robust market participation rather than a blind safety net [E23, E24].

Conceded: [E17]. The bull's dismissal of the promoter sell-off ignores that insider divestment is broad-based, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings also dropping significantly year-over-year [E14, E15, E16]. While the bull points to robust return metrics and EV/EBITDA multiples to justify a premium, it glosses over a concerning price-to-book ratio of 4.56x against a paltry sector benchmark of 2.08x [E6, E8, E9, E10]. Furthermore, celebrating a high relative strength and moving average alignment [E23, E24] disregards high annualised volatility of 54.8% and a track record of severe drawdowns reaching -38.1% [E26, E27]. The bull also minimizes the Q1 margin distortion [E54] by looking past an inconsistent quarterly operating margin trend [E13] and an explicit flag that the stock trades below its discounted cash flow value [E37]. Finally, the expansion into Dubai remains stalled due to geopolitical conflicts and ongoing wars [E62], rendering ambitious growth narratives vulnerable to external shocks.

See, there was a change in inventory method from FIFO to WAC method. There was some unrealized gain which was locked in the inventory of last year, which got spilled in this current year.
